releases.title: collectZ v3.24.5
releases.status: implementation and local verification complete; hosted release gates pending after push
releases.summary: This release makes the active workspace integration row authoritative for provider saves and Plex automation. It removes silent installation-row Plex credential fallback, persists workspace Plex reconciliation/readback/writeback controls, and sends the Core/homelab provider screen to the active workspace endpoint.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Workspace integration saves now persist Plex reconciliation, watched/rating readback, and rating/watch-state writeback controls.
Plex scheduler enablement and cadence are resolved from enabled workspace integration rows unless an explicit environment override is present.
Scheduled Plex work filters out workspaces that have not enabled the corresponding automation.
Workspace Plex execution no longer fills missing URL, credential, or section values from installation row `id=1`.
Core/homelab provider settings and Plex writeback readback use `/api/spaces/{id}/integrations` for the active workspace.
OpenAPI now documents all implemented workspace provider diagnostic endpoints and the Plex automation/writeback request and response fields.
Added focused source and Docker runtime coverage for workspace persistence, unchanged installation state, and workspace-derived scheduler configuration.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.4
releases.status: local implementation and verification complete; hosted gates pending
releases.summary: This release fixes Plex webhook receiver persistence by making the receiver belong to the same workspace integration row as its Plex connection. Save and refresh now retain Enabled state and masked URL readback, and incoming events carry the correct workspace and library into durable jobs.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Workspace Plex webhook controls now call `/api/spaces/{id}/integrations` endpoints for generation, rotation, validation, and revocation.
Workspace integration GET and PUT responses shape receiver status from their own scoped row.
Plex Now Playing display-token generation/revocation and display-preference saves now use the same workspace integration endpoint and row.
Public Now Playing display tokens resolve the scoped row that owns the token, so readback uses that workspace's Plex connection.
Incoming tokens resolve across scoped integration rows instead of checking only installation row `id=1`.
Delivery diagnostics update the row that authenticated the receiver.
Actionable webhook jobs include `spaceId` and `libraryId`, and duplicate suppression includes workspace identity.
Added a focused Docker runtime smoke covering Generate, reload, Save, delivery diagnostics, scoped job enqueue, and Revoke.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.3
releases.summary: This release makes Plex an active inbound source by accepting its documented multipart webhooks, processing new-title/watched/rating events through durable jobs, and enabling scheduled reconciliation and state readback as a fallback.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added bounded multipart parsing for Plex's JSON `payload` field and optional thumbnail.
Kept token authentication ahead of body parsing and discarded thumbnail bytes after request handling.
Queued `library.new`, `media.scrobble`, and `media.rate` events durably with queued/running duplicate suppression.
Reused the existing single-rating-key import for newly added Plex titles.
Made watched and rating events read current state from Plex before applying it to matching CollectZ rows.
Added redacted accepted/rejected delivery diagnostics to the Plex Webhook settings readback.
Enabled reconciliation and watched/rating readback for existing configured Plex integrations and made completed new connections default to active inbound monitoring.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.2
releases.status: implementation complete; hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: This release carries structured Blu-ray.com browser captures through review into canonical movie fallbacks, physical-edition evidence, identifiers, ownership formats, and a guarded used-price valuation.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a server-derived import mapping and compact, plain-text preview for supported browser captures.
Used captured year and runtime as provider-enrichment hints while preserving canonical movie release-date semantics.
Merged captured Blu-ray, 4K UHD, DVD, and digital ownership formats without removing formats already owned.
Added an idempotent Blu-ray.com physical variant keyed by canonical media row and Blu-ray.com product ID.
Stored the full physical-release evidence, including technical specs, ratings, release date, links, pricing, and original page metadata, in the variant record.
Stored IMDb and ASIN identities in media metadata.
Mapped the Blu-ray.com used-from amount to the low estimated value with currency, source, and observation time.
Preserved manual and unrelated valuations instead of silently overwriting them.
Paired collectZ `3.24.2` with browser extension `0.1.1`, which emits structured Blu-ray.com pricing while retaining the original Price text.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.1
releases.status: implementation complete; hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: This release lets a title-only browser-extension capture complete Capture Inbox review as a normal library import after the reviewer chooses its media type.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a compact library-type selector and explicit Add to library action for titled captures without lookup matches.
Added Book, Comic, Movie, TV, Audio, and Game as supported review-import targets.
Reused the existing media enrichment, deduplication, creation, and linking pipeline.
Kept the stored capture title authoritative during title-only review imports.
Recorded the chosen object type and title-review import provenance on converted captures.
Documented the title-only capture-review API contract and added backend and browser regression coverage.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.0
releases.status: implementation complete; hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: This release restores CollectZ to an upstream-supported runtime baseline by moving the backend, active CI jobs, and operational Node helper images from end-of-life Node 20 to Node 24 LTS.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Moved the production backend Docker image to Node 24.
Declared Node 24 as the supported backend package engine.
Made the production backend image use lockfile-strict `npm ci`.
Aligned active GitHub Actions jobs and scheduled dependency reporting on Node 24.
Moved the syslog collector and sizing helper images to Node 24.
Added source-contract coverage that rejects active Node 20 runtime or CI configuration.
Updated newly disclosed vulnerable transitive development/build dependencies without changing the application dependency architecture.
Repaired a stale browser fixture and pre-existing maintained-source CodeQL findings exposed by the full release gate.
Kept the current application architecture: Node/Express/Postgres for the backend and Vite-built static assets served by Nginx for the frontend.

releases.title: collectZ v3.23.21
releases.summary: This patch gives CollectZ an explicit web-app identity so an iOS Home Screen installation owns the full site instead of treating the page used during installation as its return destination.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a web app manifest with a root app identity and route scope.
Set `/dashboard` as the stable Home Screen launch URL while keeping every CollectZ route inside the installed app.
Added standalone display, theme, and Apple Home Screen metadata.
Reused the existing CollectZ mark and color palette for standard, maskable, and Apple touch icons.
Added browser coverage for the manifest contract, MIME type, metadata links, and install icon responses.
Updated Axios to `1.18.1` in backend and frontend and refreshed backend's transitive `body-parser` to `2.3.0` after newly published advisories surfaced during the release audit.
Repaired the frontend lockfile's missing optional `@emnapi` peer entries and aligned dependency CI with the supported runtime split: Node 20 for backend installs and Node 24 for frontend installs.

releases.title: collectZ v3.23.20
releases.summary: This patch removes signed, numbered-print, and event-acquisition pills from Art poster cards. Cards now keep the artwork and title dominant with at most two quiet plain-text metadata lines.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Replaced the combined numbered/signed/medium subtitle with a plain `medium · edition` line.
Added one optional plain signer line using `Signed by artist`.
Kept `Signed` on the first line only when an item is signed but no signer name is known.
Removed collectible trait pills, including event/vendor/booth context, from Art poster cards.
Kept complete collectible and acquisition metadata in existing list and detail surfaces.
Extended mobile browser coverage to verify the two-line contract, absence of trait/event pills, and viewport containment.

releases.title: collectZ v3.23.19
releases.summary: This patch keeps long collectible-detail labels inside narrow Art poster cards. On iPhone-sized screens, signing and event-acquisition labels now truncate within their own card instead of overlapping the neighboring card or widening the page beyond the viewport.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Allowed shared poster cards to shrink below the intrinsic width of their metadata.
Constrained trait-pill containers and individual pills to the available card width.
Preserved the existing two-column mobile Art grid and full trait text through the pill title/readback.
Added a mobile browser regression that checks both card-boundary containment and document viewport width with a deliberately long signer label.

releases.title: collectZ v3.23.18
releases.summary: This patch fixes scanner barcode lookups for console games that generic UPC providers describe with retail listing titles. Game-shaped UPC results such as Nintendo 3DS listings are now typed as games instead of falling through to movie matching.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added barcode-provider game inference for common console/platform terms including Nintendo 3DS, Switch, Wii, PlayStation, Xbox, Game Boy, and PC game listings.
Cleaned game retail suffixes such as platform tags, `Pre-Played`, and color/listing noise before provider enrichment search.
Preserved platform metadata on scanner lookup matches so imported game records can retain the detected console.
Treated Capture Inbox `other` media type as unknown during scanner lookup instead of forcing a concrete media type before provider normalization can infer one.
Made the scanner API smoke deterministic without requiring TMDB configuration for the existing UPC title-variant check.
